1	"""grokking_optimizers.compile — Targeted per-(optimizer, model, arch) build
2	with a portable AOT-then-JIT cache, YAML-driven search space, Bayesian
3	or Exhaustive autotune, optional PGO, and runtime-split AOT/JIT
4	subprocesses.
5	
6	This is the development-time companion to ``setup.py``. Where
7	``pip install -e .`` builds the full ``grokking_optimizers._ops``
8	extension with default flags, this module compiles a focused,
9	**maximally optimised** build for a single ``(optimizer, model, arch)``
10	triple. The pipeline is split into two halves so a CPU-only host can
11	do the heavy AOT compile and ship a cache file to the target GPU host,
12	which then does the JIT autotune sweep.
13	
14	Two-phase pipeline
15	==================
16	
17	**AOT phase (any host with the toolchain — no GPU required).**
18	
19	  1. Resolve sources for the chosen arch (bindings + every launcher +
20	     every model TU).
21	  2. Hash the source set, the host cflags, the device cflags, the
22	     resolved search-space, and the PGO state. Look up
23	     ``(optimizer, model, arch)`` in the cache. If all hashes match an
24	     entry with ``aot_completed_at != None`` and ``pgo_enabled`` agrees
25	     and the recorded artefact still exists → **cache hit**.
26	  3. Otherwise build with ``torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`` (ninja,
27	     ``MAX_JOBS=$(nproc)``, sccache wiring when on PATH), arch-tuned
28	     codegen + LTO + perf flags, and the ``SG_BUILD_*`` macros so
29	     headers can ``#if`` out unused specialisations.
30	  4. If ``--pgo`` is set, the AOT phase runs the 3-pass loop:
31	       instrument → workload → use. The PGO state is recorded so
32	       subsequent runs short-circuit when the workload hash matches.
33	  5. Record the artefact path, size, mtime, and SHA-256 in the cache.
34	     Mark ``aot_completed_at``. Save cache to disk.
35	
36	**JIT autotune phase (target GPU only).**
37	
38	  1. Load the resolved search space — by default, the COMPLETE programmatic
39	     space from build_full_search_space() (~billions of candidates per arch).
40	     Override with --search-space <path/to/your.yaml> to use a smaller
41	     curated space.
42	     Generate the cartesian product → apply static pre-filter rules →
43	     log the elimination count.
44	  2. Two autotune modes:
45	       - ``--mode exhaustive``: every survivor is built and timed.
46	         Cache is written every N trials so a Ctrl-C is recoverable.
47	       - ``--mode bayesian`` (default): Optuna TPE for ``--bayesian-trials``
48	         iterations + top-K refinement with ±2-step neighbours. The
49	         Optuna study persists to ``<cache_dir>/optuna_<opt>_<model>_<arch>.db``
50	         for cross-run resume.
51	  3. Timing is done by a **persistent subprocess worker** that holds a
52	     warm CUDA / HIP context for the full sweep, using CUDA-graph
53	     replay where the kernel supports it. Per-variant timeout falls
54	     back to one-shot subprocess timing on worker crash.
55	  4. Pick the winning combo (lowest median ms). Set ``cache.tuned_config``.
56	     Mark ``jit_completed_at``.
57	  5. Rewrite ``csrc/algorithms/tuned_configs.h`` with the winning
58	     macros so downstream consumers (setup.py builds, IDE Intellisense)
59	     pick up the tuned defaults.
60	  6. Rebuild the primary artefact with the tuned configs baked in.
61	
62	Runtime split
63	=============
64	``--runtime {aot, jit, both}`` controls which subprocesses run.
65	``both`` (default) spawns an AOT subprocess (CPU-only env) followed by
66	a JIT subprocess (GPU env). Each subprocess re-enters ``main`` with
67	the single-phase flag and reads/writes the same on-disk cache. This
68	means AOT and JIT can be tuned independently (env vars, library
69	versions, memory limits) without their settings bleeding into each
70	other. ``--aot-only`` / ``--jit-only`` remain as aliases.
71	
72	Cache schema v4
73	===============
74	The on-disk format is JSON; ``CACHE_VERSION == 4``. Forward-compatible
75	with v2 + v3 (auto-migrated on load). See ``INTERFACES.md`` for the
76	full shape. Headline additions over v2:
77	
78	    mode                 "exhaustive" | "bayesian" | None
79	    pgo_enabled          bool
80	    pgo_profile_dir      str | None
81	    pgo_workload_hash    str | None
82	    pgo_completed_at     str | None
83	    pgo_host             host dict
84	    search_space_hash    str (SHA-256 of resolved YAML space)
85	    bayesian_trials      [trial_record, …]   (stage="tpe" | "refine")
86	
87	Per-entry hashes (``source_hash``, ``host_cflags_hash``,
88	``device_cflags_hash``, ``search_space_hash``, plus ``pgo_enabled``)
89	all gate AOT freshness; any change invalidates the entry.
90	
91	Usage
92	=====
93	
94	CLI::
95	
96	    # End-to-end on a GPU host (AOT + Bayesian JIT autotune + profile)
97	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
98	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
99	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json \\
100	        --mode bayesian --bayesian-trials 500
101	
102	    # AOT-only on a CPU host with PGO (ships the cache)
103	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
104	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
105	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json --aot-only --pgo \\
106	        --pgo-workload scripts/pgo_workload.py --pgo-steps 1000 \\
107	        --aot-artifact-dir build/compiled/aot_artifacts
108	
109	    # JIT autotune only on the GPU host (consumes the cache)
110	    python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \\
111	        --optimizer supergrok2 --model mamba --arch sm_90 \\
112	        --cache build/.compile_cache.json --jit-only --mode exhaustive
113	
114	Importable::
115	
116	    from grokking_optimizers.compile import build, build_aot, build_jit, CompileCache
117	    cache = CompileCache(Path("build/.compile_cache.json"))
118	    so_path = build(optimizer="supergrok2", model="mamba", arch="sm_90",
119	                    cache=cache, autotune_mode="bayesian",
120	                    bayesian_trials=None,  # None = multi-criterion auto-stop

475	#
476	# For each CUDA arch we emit two -gencode flags:
477	#   1. compute_XX[a],code=sm_XX[a]  — SASS for the target SM
478	#   2. compute_XX,code=compute_XX   — PTX fallback so older drivers can JIT
479	#      forward to newer hardware that didn't exist at compile time.
480	# The "a" suffix on Hopper+ tells NVCC to emit arch-specific instructions
481	# (TMA, wgmma, tcgen05 etc.) that the non-"a" variant rejects.

483	# SASS-only gencode toggle. When True, _nvcc_gencode_pair emits ONLY the
484	# ``code=sm_NN`` SASS gencode and DROPS the ``compute_NN`` PTX-fallback
485	# gencode. For an arch that ships a real kernel body (sm_90 / gfx942 today)
486	# this shrinks the fatbin and skips the JIT-from-PTX path entirely on the
487	# exact target SM. It is OFF by default because dropping the PTX fallback
488	# means the binary cannot JIT-forward onto a newer, not-yet-existing SM — so
489	# it's only safe when you are certain of the deployment GPU. Set via

494	def _nvcc_gencode_pair(num: int, suffix: str = "",
495	                       sass_only: Optional[bool] = None) -> List[str]:
496	    """Return the -gencode flags for a CUDA arch.
497	
498	    By default emits the SASS gencode + a ``compute_NN`` PTX-fallback gencode
499	    (so older drivers can JIT-forward onto newer hardware). When
500	    ``sass_only`` (defaulting to the module-level ``_SASS_ONLY_GENCODE``) is
501	    True, the PTX fallback is dropped — smaller fatbin / no JIT — which is
502	    only safe for archs whose exact SM is the known deployment target.
503	    """
504	    if sass_only is None:
505	        sass_only = _SASS_ONLY_GENCODE
506	    sm = f"sm_{num}{suffix}"
507	    compute = f"compute_{num}{suffix}"
508	    compute_fallback = f"compute_{num}"   # PTX fallback is always non-"a"
509	    flags = [f"-gencode=arch={compute},code={sm}"]
510	    if not sass_only:
511	        flags.append(
512	            f"-gencode=arch={compute_fallback},code={compute_fallback}")
513	    return flags

1177	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1178	# Programmatic search-space builder — the COMPLETE space, not a curated list
1179	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1180	#
1181	# Earlier revisions of this file embedded a hand-written YAML blob with a
1182	# small curated set of values per tuning dimension (e.g. block ∈ {64, 128,
1183	# 256, 512, 1024}). That biased the autotuner — Bayesian TPE could only
1184	# sample what we'd pre-decided was "reasonable". This was a mistake: the
1185	# whole point of an extensive optimization run is to discover non-obvious
1186	# winners, and pre-curating values defeats that.
1187	#
1188	# build_full_search_space() now generates the search space programmatically
1189	# from hardware specs:
1190	#   - every warp-aligned (sm_90) / wavefront-aligned (gfx942) block size
1191	#   - the full range of vector widths the load/store instructions support
1192	#   - every power-of-2 unroll factor up to a generous cap
1193	#   - every valid pipeline depth, register-budget, cluster shape, etc.
1194	#
1195	# The result is a Cartesian product of ~10⁹ candidates per arch — far too
1196	# many to materialize. Three consequences:
1197	#   1. ``cartesian()`` is now a generator (was a list).
1198	#   2. ``cartesian_count(space, arch)`` returns the size without iteration.
1199	#   3. ``ss_prefilter()`` accepts an iterable and streams survivors.
1200	# Bayesian TPE doesn't care about the size — it samples one config at a
1201	# time using the per-dim value lists. Exhaustive mode streams every survivor
1202	# via iter_prefilter (UNCAPPED — the full feasible space; see _run_exhaustive).
1203	#
1204	# Users can still override the entire space via --search-space <path.yaml>.
1205	
1206	
1207	def _dim(name: str, dtype: str, values: List[Any], macro: Optional[str],
1208	         applies_to: List[str], kind: str = "macro") -> Dict[str, Any]:
1209	    """One tuning dimension.
1210	
1211	    ``kind`` is one of:
1212	      - ``"macro"`` (default): becomes a ``-DSG_TUNED_*=VAL`` flag passed to nvcc/hipcc.
1213	      - ``"pallas_kwarg"``: passed as a keyword argument to ``pl.pallas_call``.
1214	      - ``"nvcc_flag"`` / ``"hipcc_flag"``: promoted to a bare compiler flag
1215	        (handled out-of-band, e.g. ``maxrregcount``).
1216	    """
1217	    return {"name": name, "type": dtype, "values": values,
1218	            "macro": macro, "applies_to": applies_to, "kind": kind}

1221	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1222	# Live vs. dead tuning dimensions
1223	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1224	#
1225	# A producer→consumer audit of the emitted ``-DSG_TUNED_*`` macros against the
1226	# committed kernel bodies (grep of every *.cu / *.hip.cpp) showed that of the
1227	# ~22 macros the autotuner can emit, only FIVE are ever ``#ifdef``'d / read by
1228	# any kernel:
1229	#
1230	#   SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE  (11 consumers)   — live
1231	#   SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH   (11 consumers)   — live
1232	#   SG_TUNED_UNROLL      (11 consumers)   — live
1233	#   SG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH (12 consumers)   — live  (kernel clamps to [1,4])
1234	#   SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE (2 consumers)  — live
1235	#
1236	# ``maxrregcount`` carries ``macro=None`` and is emitted as a real
1237	# ``--maxrregcount=N`` / ``-amdgpu-max-num-vgprs=N`` compiler flag, so it
1238	# genuinely changes the produced binary and is LIVE even though it is not an
1239	# SG_TUNED macro. All Pallas dims (kind == "pallas_kwarg") are real
1240	# ``pl.pallas_call`` arguments and are likewise LIVE.
1241	#
1242	# Every OTHER SG_TUNED_* / *_ENABLED macro (NUM_STAGES, SWIZZLE,
1243	# TMA_DESCRIPTORS, WGMMA_SHAPE, WARP_SPECIALIZATION, FP8/FP4_LAYOUT,
1244	# TCGEN05_VARIANT, LDS_PADDING, WAVES_PER_EU, MFMA_SHAPE, FP8/FP4_MFMA_LAYOUT,
1245	# SCHEDULER_HINT, WMMA_SHAPE, DPP_MODIFIER, TGSPLIT, the bare TMA bool) is
1246	# DEAD: no kernel reads it, so every distinct value produces a
1247	# binary-IDENTICAL artifact. Leaving these in the search space (a) inflates the
1248	# Cartesian product by ~10^4× on sm_90 / sm_100, wasting the sampler's trial
1249	# budget on binary-identical configs, and (b) poisons ``config_key`` so two
1250	# binary-identical configs hash to different keys → false cache misses → full
1251	# recompiles.
1252	#
1253	# We keep the macros *emittable* (the dims stay in the space, the
1254	# ``resolve_macros`` / ``resolve_extra_*_flags`` paths are untouched) so a dead
1255	# dim can be revived later by simply moving its name into ``_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS``.
1256	# But for now each dead dim is PINNED to a single default value (so it stops
1257	# expanding the search space) and DROPPED from ``config_key`` (so binary-
1258	# identical configs collapse to one cache entry).
1259	
1260	# Names of dims that change the emitted binary (live SG_TUNED macros + the
1261	# real --maxrregcount flag). Pallas kwargs are handled separately by kind.
1262	_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS: frozenset = frozenset({
1263	    "block", "vec", "unroll", "async_depth", "cluster_shape", "maxrregcount",
1264	})
1265	
1266	# Hard ceiling for the async-copy pipeline depth. The committed kernels clamp
1267	# SG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH to [1, 4] (cp.async / async-pipeline stage count); the
1268	# search formerly offered [1, 16], so values 5..16 produced a kernel
1269	# byte-identical to the depth-4 build yet forced a fresh (wasted) compile.
1270	_ASYNC_DEPTH_MAX: int = 4
1271	
1272	
1273	_KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE: Optional[frozenset] = None
1274	
1275	
1276	def _kernel_source_macros() -> frozenset:
1277	    """Auto-detect which ``SG_TUNED_*`` macros the committed kernel bodies
1278	    actually read. Scans the device-source trees (csrc/ + kernels/) once
1279	    (cached) and returns the set of macro tokens found. The search-space builder
1280	    uses this to decide which tuning dims are LIVE — so the space self-adjusts to
1281	    whatever the kernels honor, instead of relying on a hand-maintained
1282	    producer→consumer audit that drifts the moment a kernel gains or loses an
1283	    ``#ifdef``.
1284	
1285	    Returns an EMPTY set if no source tree is visible (e.g. an installed wheel
1286	    without csrc/); callers then fall back to the hardcoded floor.
1287	    """
1288	    global _KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE
1289	    if _KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE is not None:
1290	        return _KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE
1291	    import re as _re
1292	    roots = [REPO_ROOT / "csrc", REPO_ROOT / "grokking_optimizers" / "kernels"]
1293	    pat = _re.compile(r"SG_TUNED_[A-Z0-9_]+")
1294	    exts = {".cu", ".cuh", ".h", ".hpp", ".hip", ".cpp", ".cc", ".cxx"}
1295	    found: set = set()
1296	    for root in roots:
1297	        if not root.exists():
1298	            continue
1299	        for p in root.rglob("*"):
1300	            if p.suffix in exts:
1301	                try:
1302	                    found.update(pat.findall(p.read_text(errors="ignore")))
1303	                except OSError:
1304	                    continue
1305	    _KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE = frozenset(found)
1306	    return _KERNEL_MACRO_CACHE

1309	def _is_dead_dim(spec: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
1310	    """True if ``spec`` is a tuning dim whose value never reaches the binary.
1311	
1312	    A dim is LIVE (not dead) when sweeping it actually changes the emitted
1313	    machine code; otherwise sweeping it just burns compiles on byte-identical
1314	    binaries. The determination is AUTO-DERIVED from the committed kernel
1315	    sources, so the search space tracks the kernels' real tuning surface no
1316	    matter what is being compiled (rather than a hand-maintained list that can
1317	    silently go stale when a kernel adds or drops an ``#ifdef SG_TUNED_*``):
1318	
1319	      * Pallas kwargs are arguments to ``pl.pallas_call`` — always live.
1320	      * A bare compiler flag (``macro is None``, e.g. ``maxrregcount`` →
1321	        ``--maxrregcount=N``) always changes ptxas codegen — always live.
1322	      * A ``-DSG_TUNED_*`` macro dim is live iff some committed kernel actually
1323	        reads that macro (see :func:`_kernel_source_macros`). The hardcoded
1324	        ``_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS`` is only a defensive floor for the (degenerate)
1325	        case where the source scan finds nothing — e.g. a bodyless registry.
1326	    """
1327	    if spec.get("kind") == "pallas_kwarg":
1328	        return False
1329	    macro = spec.get("macro")
1330	    if macro is None:
1331	        return False  # real compiler flag (maxrregcount) — always affects code
1332	    detected = _kernel_source_macros()
1333	    if detected:
1334	        # Live iff the kernels read this macro (exact, or a derived variant
1335	        # like SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE_VOLUME for SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE).
1336	        live = macro in detected or any(t.startswith(macro + "_")
1337	                                        for t in detected)
1338	        return not live
1339	    # Source scan empty (no kernel tree visible) — fall back to the floor set.
1340	    return spec.get("name") not in _LIVE_TUNING_DIMS
1341

1343	# Dim names dropped from ``config_key`` so binary-identical configs collapse to
1344	# one cache entry. This is the union of dead-macro dim names across all
1345	# CUDA/HIP builders. ``num_stages`` is deliberately EXCLUDED here: it is a dead
1346	# device macro on CUDA/HIP (handled by pinning, below) but is ALSO a genuine,
1347	# live ``pl.pallas_call`` kwarg on Pallas archs — dropping it from the key

1358	def _pin_dead_dims(dims: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
1359	    """Collapse every DEAD tuning dim to a single pinned default value.
1360	
1361	    The dim object is preserved (so the macro is still emitted and can be
1362	    revived) but its ``values`` list is truncated to its first entry, removing
1363	    it from the Cartesian product. Mutates and returns ``dims``. Live dims and
1364	    Pallas kwargs are untouched.
1365	    """
1366	    for d in dims:
1367	        if _is_dead_dim(d):
1368	            vals = d.get("values") or []
1369	            if len(vals) > 1:
1370	                d["values"] = vals[:1]
1371	            d["live"] = False
1372	        else:
1373	            d["live"] = True
1374	    return dims

2118	# with a per-cell sweep seeded from the solver's footprint estimate for that
2119	# exact (model, optimizer, arch). The autotuner then times each cap and the
2120	# winner is whatever ptxas+silicon actually prefers for that cell.
2121	def _megakernel_maxrregcount_values(arch_key: str,
2122	                                    model: str,
2123	                                    optimizer: str) -> List[int]:
2124	    """Per-CELL register-cap sweep for a fused megakernel (model×optimizer).
2125	
2126	    Seeds the sweep around the megakernel solver's estimated L3 register
2127	    footprint for this cell: we sample the uncapped point (let ptxas choose),
2128	    the arch ceiling, and a spread of caps from the estimate down toward the
2129	    producer-warp-group floor. The autotuner times each and keeps the fastest;
2130	    a cap only wins if its spill is cold (§ knob #1).
2131	    """
2132	    entry = ARCH_TABLE[arch_key]
2133	    cap = entry.max_regs_per_thread or 255
2134	    # Lazy import to avoid a heavy import at module load (mirrors megakernel.py).
2135	    try:
2136	        from grokking_optimizers import megakernel as _mk
2137	        plan = _mk.solve(model, optimizer, arch_key if arch_key in
2138	                         _mk.MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS else _mk.MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS[0])
2139	        est = max(32, min(cap, int(plan.regs)))
2140	    except Exception as _swexc:
2141	        _debug_swallow('_megakernel_maxrregcount_values', _swexc)
2142	        est = cap  # solver unavailable → fall back to the full arch range
2143	    # Candidate caps: estimate, a few steps above/below (to bracket the real
2144	    # ptxas number), the arch ceiling, and a low cap that trades occupancy for
2145	    # registers. De-duplicate + sort; always include 0 == "no cap" (ptxas free)
2146	    # which is encoded as the arch ceiling here so the bare flag stays valid.
2147	    cands = set()
2148	    for c in (est - 16, est - 8, est, est + 8, est + 16,
2149	              (est + cap) // 2, cap):
2150	        if 24 <= c <= cap:
2151	            cands.add(c - (c % 4))  # 4-step aligned, matches _maxrregcount_values
2152	    cands.add(cap)
2153	    if cap >= 255:
2154	        cands.add(255)
2155	    return sorted(v for v in cands if v >= 24) or [cap]

2381	    """Stream the full Cartesian product as {dim_name: value} dicts.
2382

2384	    configs per arch — never call ``list(cartesian(...))`` on it. Use
2385	    ``cartesian_count()`` for the size, and pipe this iterator through
2386	    ``ss_prefilter()`` which yields survivors lazily.

2391	    if not dims:
2392	        return
2393	    names = [d["name"] for d in dims]
2394	    values = [d["values"] for d in dims]
2395	    for combo in itertools.product(*values):
2396	        cfg: Dict[str, Any] = {}
2397	        for n, v in zip(names, combo):
2398	            cfg[n] = tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v

Now I have the key §6 evidence. Let me note this critical finding:

[§6] L3106-3162 `cuda_graph_median_ms` + L3259-3307 `_bg_cuda_graph_median_ms` (in worker body): both use `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()` + `torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side_stream)` to capture `opt.step()` then `graph.replay()` for timing. This is the TIMING harness. CRITICAL: it captures `opt.step()` — the optimizer's Python-level step which dispatches to the kernel. KEY QUESTION for owner: if the megakernel is a persistent kernel with grid-wide barriers/cooperative-groups launch, `torch.cuda.graph` capture may FAIL (cooperative launch + graph capture interaction). Note: `_time_with_graph` (L3310-3316) wraps the graph timing in try/except returning `None` on failure, and there's a fallback `_time_with_events` (L3319) — so if graph capture fails for the megakernel, it silently falls back to event timing. This is measurement-harness-only (graph object never feeds an execution path), but the fallback masks whether megakernel variants can even be graph-captured.

[§4] L3315 `except Exception: return None` in `_time_with_graph` — swallows ALL exceptions from graph timing silently (no logging), then falls back. This means a megakernel that can't be graph-captured would silently use event timing without any indication. Combined with `use_graph` toggle logic I need to read next.

TimingWorker is well-engineered with watchdog. Let me note findings:

[§4-bug] L3959-3985 `_read_line` reads ONE CHARACTER AT A TIME with `self._proc.stdout.read(1)` in a busy-wait loop with `_time.sleep(0.01)`. This is a correctness-safe but inefficient pattern; for high-throughput timing it adds latency. Since reads are JSON lines and results are infrequent (one per variant timed), the 10ms poll granularity is the bottleneck on small kernels. Could be §1 optimization (low impact since GPU timing dominates).

[§4-race] L3893-3901 `time()` holds `_io_lock` for write+read. The watchdog `ping()` also takes `_io_lock`. Good - serialized. But note: `_read_line` is called inside the lock with `timeout=self.timeout` (180s default). If a variant hangs, the watchdog can't ping (lock held) for up to 180s, and the `time()` call's own `_last_pong_ts` refresh won't happen. The watchdog grace is 60s, so it would want to kill, but it's blocked on `_io_lock`. Let me note: watchdog `ping` would block on `_io_lock` during a long `time()` — meaning the SIGKILL path can't fire while a hung variant holds the lock. Actually `_force_restart` uses `_watchdog_lock` not `_io_lock`, but `ping()` (which determines staleness) takes `_io_lock`. So a hung 180s variant blocks pings. This is a real watchdog-defeat smell. Let me flag as unconfirmed pending deeper read of the staleness logic.

Actually, re-reading: the watchdog loop at L3818 calls `self.ping()` which tries to acquire `_io_lock`. If `time()` holds it for 180s, `ping()` blocks there, so the watchdog thread is stuck and can't reach the age check at L3825. So a wedged GPU mid-`time()` won't be detected until the 180s timeout returns. That defeats the 60s grace for the specific case of a hang during timing (vs a hang between timings). Flag it.

MultiGPUTimingPool is well-built with work-stealing. Let me note:

[§4-bug] L4285-4303 `MultiGPUTimingPool.time()` calls `fut.result()` with NO timeout — blocks indefinitely. If the only worker dies after the item was dequeued by its dispatcher but before `fut.set_result`, the future never completes. The dispatcher's `try/finally` sets exception on failure (L4271-4276), so that's covered. But if `time()` is called when `self.workers` is non-empty but all dispatchers have exited (e.g. after `stop()`), the item sits in the queue forever and `fut.result()` hangs. Edge case — flag low.

5121	class BayesianEarlyStopper:
5122	    """Multi-criterion stopper for Optuna autotune.
5123	
5124	    Stops when ANY of the following triggers (whichever fires first):
5125	      (a) Best-so-far plateau: no improvement > ``min_delta_rel`` for
5126	          ``patience`` trials.
5127	      (b) EI exhaustion: rolling EI estimate (mean of per-trial relative
5128	          improvements over the trailing ``patience`` window) falls below
5129	          ``ei_floor``. Empirical proxy: TPE doesn't expose Optuna's
5130	          acquisition value, so we measure the rate at which new trials
5131	          beat the running best.
5132	      (c) Coverage saturation: new-(dim_name, value) tuples per trial
5133	          < ``coverage_growth_floor``.
5134	      (d) Wall-clock budget: ``time.time() - start_time > max_seconds``.
5135	      (e) Hard ceiling: ``trial_count >= max_trials`` — a SAFETY RAIL only
5136	          (default 1M). Mandate #13: this is NOT the primary stopping lever;
5137	          (a)/(b)/(c) govern convergence so the cap is essentially never the
5138	          binding constraint. Lifting it is unnecessary — broad coverage is
5139	          the sampler's job, not exhaustive enumeration.
5140	    """
5141	
5142	    def __init__(self, *,
5143	                 min_delta_rel: float = _DEFAULT_MIN_DELTA_REL,
5144	                 patience: Optional[int] = None,
5145	                 ei_floor: float = _DEFAULT_EI_FLOOR,
5146	                 coverage_growth_floor: float = _DEFAULT_COVERAGE_GROWTH_FLOOR,
5147	                 max_seconds: Optional[float] = None,
5148	                 max_trials: int = _DEFAULT_STOPPER_SAFETY_CAP):
5149	        self.min_delta_rel = min_delta_rel
5150	        self._patience_override = patience  # None → auto = max(50, 0.1*N)
5151	        self.ei_floor = ei_floor
5152	        self.coverage_growth_floor = coverage_growth_floor
5153	        self.max_seconds = max_seconds
5154	        self.max_trials = max_trials
5155	        self.start_time = time.time()
5156	        self.best = math.inf
5157	        self.last_improve_trial = 0
5158	        self.coverage_set: set = set()  # (dim_name, value) tuples
5159	        self.coverage_history: List[int] = []  # cumulative |coverage_set| per trial
5160	        self.trial_count = 0
5161	        self.stop_reason: Optional[str] = None
5162	        # (b) EI exhaustion: per-trial relative improvements over the
5163	        # running best. Kept unbounded; should_stop() slices the trailing
5164	        # ``self.patience`` window (patience is dynamic when auto-mode).
5165	        self._improvement_window: collections.deque = collections.deque()
5166	        # Cached for to_dict() / cache persistence.
5167	        self._last_ei_estimate: Optional[float] = None
5168	        # (f) Stream C — cost-model rejection budget. Incremented every
5169	        # time the learned cost model prunes a candidate before it gets
5170	        # measured. Used by should_stop() to detect that the model is
5171	        # vetoing most TPE suggestions AND the best timing has plateaued,
5172	        # which is a stronger stopping signal than plateau alone.
5173	        self._cost_model_rejections: int = 0
5174	
5175	    @property
5176	    def patience(self) -> int:
5177	        if self._patience_override is not None:
5178	            return self._patience_override
5179	        return max(50, self.trial_count // 10)
5180	
5181	    def observe(self, trial_value: float, trial_params: Dict[str, Any],
5182	                *, was_pruned_by_cost_model: bool = False) -> None:
5183	        self.trial_count += 1
5184	        prev_best = self.best
5185	        # (b) EI estimate: per-trial relative improvement over prev_best.
5186	        # First trial (prev_best == inf) records 0 — nothing to improve over.
5187	        # Non-finite trials (failed/infeasible) record 0 — no signal.
5188	        if math.isfinite(trial_value) and math.isfinite(prev_best):
5189	            improvement = max(
5190	                0.0,
5191	                (prev_best - trial_value) / max(abs(prev_best), 1e-12),
5192	            )
5193	        else:
5194	            improvement = 0.0
5195	        self._improvement_window.append(improvement)
5196	        # Plateau tracking — only count finite improvements as such.
5197	        if math.isfinite(trial_value) and \
5198	                trial_value < self.best * (1 - self.min_delta_rel):
5199	            self.best = trial_value
5200	            self.last_improve_trial = self.trial_count
5201	        # Coverage tracking
5202	        for k, v in trial_params.items():
5203	            self.coverage_set.add((k, _hashable(v)))
5204	        self.coverage_history.append(len(self.coverage_set))
5205	        # (f) Stream C — bump the cost-model rejection counter when the
5206	        # caller flags this trial as having been pruned by the learned
5207	        # cost model. should_stop() uses this counter to detect that
5208	        # the model is vetoing most candidates AND the best has plateaued.
5209	        if was_pruned_by_cost_model:
5210	            self._cost_model_rejections += 1
5211	
5212	    def should_stop(self) -> bool:
5213	        if self.stop_reason is not None:
5214	            return True
5215	        # (e) hard ceiling
5216	        if self.trial_count >= self.max_trials:
5217	            self.stop_reason = f"hard_ceiling:{self.max_trials}"
5218	            return True
5219	        # (d) wall-clock
5220	        if self.max_seconds is not None:
5221	            elapsed = time.time() - self.start_time
5222	            if elapsed >= self.max_seconds:
5223	                self.stop_reason = f"max_seconds:{int(elapsed)}s"
5224	                return True
5225	        # Need a warm-up of at least patience+10 trials before other criteria fire
5226	        if self.trial_count < self.patience + 10:
5227	            return False
5228	        # (a) best-so-far plateau
5229	        if (self.trial_count - self.last_improve_trial) >= self.patience:
5230	            self.stop_reason = f"plateau:no_improvement_in_{self.patience}"
5231	            return True
5232	        # (c) coverage saturation: growth over last `patience` trials
5233	        if len(self.coverage_history) >= self.patience:
5234	            window_growth = (self.coverage_history[-1]
5235	                             - self.coverage_history[-self.patience])
5236	            growth_rate = window_growth / max(1, self.patience)
5237	            if growth_rate < self.coverage_growth_floor:
5238	                self.stop_reason = (
5239	                    f"coverage_saturated:growth_rate={growth_rate:.4f}")
5240	                return True
5241	        # (b) EI exhaustion: empirical EI = mean of relative improvements
5242	        # over the trailing ``patience`` window. ei_floor <= 0 disables the
5243	        # criterion (user can opt out while keeping other stoppers active).
5244	        if self.ei_floor > 0 and len(self._improvement_window) >= self.patience:
5245	            recent = list(self._improvement_window)[-self.patience:]
5246	            rolling_mean = sum(recent) / max(1, len(recent))
5247	            self._last_ei_estimate = rolling_mean
5248	            if rolling_mean < self.ei_floor:
5249	                self.stop_reason = f"ei_exhausted:{rolling_mean:.2e}"
5250	                return True
5251	        # (f) Stream C — cost-model rejection budget exhausted. When the
5252	        # learned cost model has been rejecting >60% of TPE suggestions
5253	        # AND the best timing has plateaued for at least half the
5254	        # patience window, we can stop earlier than the plateau-alone
5255	        # criterion would allow: the model has already convinced itself
5256	        # there's nothing better to find. Only fires after a generous
5257	        # warm-up (50 trials minimum) so we don't trip on cold-start
5258	        # variance.
5259	        if (self.trial_count >= max(50, self.patience)
5260	                and self._cost_model_rejections > 0.6 * self.trial_count
5261	                and (self.trial_count - self.last_improve_trial)
5262	                    >= self.patience // 2):
5263	            self.stop_reason = (
5264	                f"cost_model_rejection_exhausted:"
5265	                f"{self._cost_model_rejections}/{self.trial_count}")
5266	            return True
5267	        return False

5291	def _detect_topk_elbow(records: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
5292	    """Detect the elbow in a sorted-by-timing trial list.
5293	
5294	    Sort successful records by ``timing_ms`` (ascending), compute the
5295	    second discrete differences over the timing series, return the index
5296	    where the curvature peaks (i.e. the knee where good trials end and
5297	    long-tail trials begin). Capped at 50 and at len(records).
5298	
5299	    Fallback: ``min(50, len(records) // 4)`` when there's too little
5300	    data to fit a curvature estimate or all timings are degenerate.
5301	    """
5302	    ok = [r for r in records if (r.get("status") == "ok"
5303	                                  or r.get("timing_ms") is not None)]
5304	    n = len(ok)
5305	    if n == 0:
5306	        return 0
5307	    if n < 5:
5308	        return min(50, max(1, n))
5309	    # Extract timings (records may use 'timing_ms' or 'value_ms')
5310	    def _val(r):
5311	        v = r.get("timing_ms")
5312	        if v is None:
5313	            v = r.get("value_ms")
5314	        return float(v) if v is not None else math.inf
5315	    times = sorted(_val(r) for r in ok)
5316	    times = [t for t in times if math.isfinite(t)]
5317	    if len(times) < 5:
5318	        return min(50, max(1, len(times) or 1))
5319	    # Second discrete differences: t[i-1] - 2*t[i] + t[i+1]
5320	    d2 = [times[i - 1] - 2.0 * times[i] + times[i + 1]
5321	          for i in range(1, len(times) - 1)]
5322	    # times is sorted ascending, so the curve is flat ("good" configs)
5323	    # then turns sharply upward (long-tail slow configs). The knee is the
5324	    # point of maximum *positive* curvature (largest second difference) —
5325	    # i.e. where the convex up-turn is steepest. argmax(d2) finds it.
5326	    if not d2 or all(abs(x) < 1e-12 for x in d2):
5327	        return min(50, max(1, len(times) // 4))
5328	    # The knee index in the original 'times' array is d2_idx + 1
5329	    knee = max(range(len(d2)), key=lambda i: d2[i]) + 1
5330	    # Ensure at least a few seeds even if curvature is shallow
5331	    knee = max(knee, min(3, len(times)))
5332	    return min(50, knee)

The docstring at L84-89 claims `search_space_hash` "gates AOT freshness; any change invalidates the entry". But for AOT specifically, search_space_hash is recorded by `record_aot` only if passed. More importantly: the `not in (None, X)` pattern means a cached AOT entry whose search_space_hash differs ONLY invalidates if the cached value is non-None and differs. This is a deliberate looseness (None = legacy/unknown), but it means **a stale entry with search_space_hash=None never invalidates on space change**. Same pattern in `is_jit_fresh` L6489-6491. This is the documented behavior pattern but worth flagging: the search-space-hash gate is "soft" (None passes). Whether this is a bug depends on intent — file as a smell.

More critically — does AOT actually depend on the search space? AOT builds the base artifact with SG_BUILD_* macros, not SG_TUNED_* (those are JIT). The search space only affects JIT variants. So gating AOT on search_space_hash is arguably over-conservative, not under. The real question: are there flags that SHOULD invalidate but don't? Let me note: `is_aot_fresh` checks source_hash, host_cflags_hash, device_cflags_hash, pgo_enabled, pgo_workload_hash, search_space_hash. That matches the docstring claim. Good coverage. The soft-None on search_space is the only gap.

# LINE-BY-LINE REVIEW: compile.py lines 1–7000

**Coverage:** Read contiguously L1–7036, no sampling. Dead-code and cross-range claims verified repo-wide via grep/AST. The autotuner core (search spaces, prefilter, timing, cache, cost model, Bayesian stopper) got depth; boilerplate is one-lined.

## §1 — OPTIMIZATIONS of the autotuner

**HIGH — `run_bayesian` serializes a multi-GPU pool (L5579–5645).** The TPE loop is strict `study.ask()` → `timer(cfg)` → `study.tell()`: one config in flight, blocking on `fut.result()` before the next ask. I confirmed (cross-range L13210–13267) that in the DEFAULT bayesian mode the `timer` wraps `MultiGPUTimingPool` (`worker = pool` at L13214 when >1 GPU visible). So the pool's work-stealing parallelism is wasted — N-1 GPUs idle during a bayesian sweep. This contradicts the owner's hardware-saturation mandate (MEMORY.md: MPS + 14-worker fleet). Only `_run_exhaustive` could fan out. **Fix:** batch `study.ask()` (K configs) + `TPESampler(constant_liar=True)` + submit K concurrent futures to the pool, then `tell` as they complete. Root cause is in-range (the sequential loop); wiring confirmation is cross-range (see §7).

**MED — `TimingWorker._read_line` reads one byte at a time (L3959–3985).** `self._proc.stdout.read(1)` in a `sleep(0.01)` busy-loop. Adds up to ~10 ms latency per result line plus per-char syscall overhead. Negligible when GPU timing dominates (default iters=21), but on fast kernels / short sweeps it's pure overhead. **Fix:** `readline()` on the line-buffered pipe with a select/poll deadline.

**LOW — cost-model pruning is a real sweep-cost reduction when enabled** (CostModel L4618 + stopper criterion (f) L5259). Off by default. The deterministic `seed=0` (L4742) and feature-dim load guard (L4920) make it safe. Good as-is; no change needed.

**LOW — variant artifact reuse by build_sig (L6560 `get_fresh_variant`) already skips recompiles** on resumed sweeps. Solid.

## §2 — HARDCODED-VALUE VIOLATIONS

**Note:** ARCH_TABLE (L538–1090) is the *designed* single-source-of-truth; flagging it wholesale would be a false positive. The real, separable item:

**MED, load-bearing — ARCH_TABLE physical constants are vendor-spec literals, not device queries.** `l2_bytes` (L605/666/688/815 — comment literally says "verify on silicon"), `max_smem_per_block`, `warp_size`, `max_regs_per_thread`, `max_threads_per_block` are hand-entered, not from `cudaDeviceGetAttribute`/`hipDeviceGetAttribute`. For a new GPU not in the table, `_arch_l2_bytes` falls back to 64 MiB (L1152) and smem/regs to defaults — the L2-flush buffer and smem prefilter rules then use wrong sizes. Clock-locking *does* query the device (L3002 `clocks.max.sm,clocks.max.mem`) — so the pattern exists; these statics could derive the same way. Load-bearing because the flush size and smem budget change tuning behavior on an unlisted/mis-specced device.

**MED, load-bearing — prefilter rule magic constants embedded per-arch.**
- L1481 `... <= 65536` (CDNA register-file/EU) — hardcoded, not from ArchEntry.
- L1894 `(block // 64) <= 16`, L1896 `waves_per_eu * (block // 64) <= 20` (gfx942) — magic occupancy ceilings.
- L1800 `num_stages * vec <= block // 32` (sm_90).
- L1460/1478/1497 smem heuristic `block * num_stages * 4 * vec` — the `4` (fp32 bytes) is hardwired; wrong for fp16/fp8/fp4 kernels. These ride in the YAML-emitted `expr` strings, so they change which configs survive prefilter for a new dtype/arch.

**LOW–MED — cost-model feature table is a second hand-maintained dim list (L4357 `_COST_MODEL_CANONICAL_DIM_VALUES`).** Does not auto-derive from the arch search spaces (intentionally process-stable for model deserialization). A new dim (the pending 7-wgmma task) featurizes as all-zeros unless added here. The FEATURE_DIM bump auto-invalidates saved models (load guard L4920), so it's safe-but-silent. See §5.

**LOW — `_COST_MODEL_STALL_REASON_COUNT = 14` (L4429)** is a hand-maintained constant. I AST-counted `STALL_DIM_HINTS` (L27167) = exactly 14 keys, so it's currently correct. But the comment (L4426) names a self-test `cost_model_feature_dim_matches_components` that **does not exist** (grep-confirmed; `_cost_model_compute_feature_dim()` at L4411 has zero callers). So the "kept in sync" claim is false — adding a stall hint silently drifts FEATURE_DIM. Load guard prevents corruption (degrades to cold-start). Latent maintainability bug, not live.

**LOW (cosmetic) magic-as-defaults** (all overridable via constructor/BuildSpec/CLI, so not violations, but listing for completeness): `JIT_CACHE_FLUSH_EVERY=5` (L201), `QUICK_BAYESIAN_TRIALS=25` (L1170), `_MAX_HOST_HISTORY=200` (L198), 120 s pip timeout (L352), `timeout_per_variant=180`/`watchdog 30/60` (L3675/3680/3681), calibrate `ref_size=2048` (L3387/3932), `_COST_MODEL_COLD_START_FLOOR=100` (L4615), HyperbandPruner `max_resource=21` (L5344, tied to iters=21), top-K cap `50` (L5332), PGO workload `--size 2048`/`--arch sm_90`/`--model mamba` defaults (L2854–2858, informational only).

## §4 — BUGS / correctness smells

**HIGH — default PGO workload is broken (CONFIRMED by repro).** `DEFAULT_PGO_WORKLOAD = Path(__file__)` (L200) = compile.py. `collect_workload` (L14328, cross-range) execs `[python, <workload>, "--so", X, "--opt", Y, "--model", Z, "--arch", W, "--steps", N]`. That routes to `main()` (L15332), not `_pgo_workload_main()` (L2838). Repro: `python -m grokking_optimizers.compile --so /tmp/x --opt AdamW --model mamba --arch sm_90 --steps 1` →

```
error: argument --optimizer/-O: invalid choice: 'AdamW' (choose from 'adamw',...)
```

(argparse rejects `--opt AdamW` / `--so` / `--steps`; SystemExit(2), before any GPU work). `scripts/pgo_workload.py` no longer exists. **Result:** any `--pgo` run without an explicit separate `--pgo-workload <script>` fails at pass 2. Fix: add a workload sub-entry intercept in `main()` that calls `_pgo_workload_main()`, or re-point `DEFAULT_PGO_WORKLOAD`.

**MED — watchdog grace not honored during an active `time()` (L3893–3901 vs L3818).** `time()` holds `_io_lock` for write+read with `timeout=self.timeout` (180 s default). The watchdog's `ping()` (L3922) also takes `_io_lock`, so during a long/hung `time()` the watchdog blocks and can't reach the staleness check (L3825). Not an unbounded deadlock — `time()` returns None at `timeout_per_variant` — but effective hang-detection latency during timing is ≤180 s, not the intended 60 s grace. Fix: use a separate liveness channel or a non-blocking ping.

**MED, latent — prefilter eval error silently empties the survivor set (L2491–2495).** `compile_feasibility_check` catches any eval exception and `return False` (config rejected). A rule referencing a variable not in the config's dims rejects *every* config → silent total elimination. NOT triggered by the built-in spaces (rule vars match their dims), but bites the `--search-space <YAML>` path and the pending 7-dim registration (a rule naming a missing dim). This is exactly the kind of silent suppression the no-suppression mandate forbids. Fix: raise at build time on eval error, or treat eval-error as pass-through.

**LOW–MED — cache `search_space_hash` soft-None gate (docstring/code drift, L6472/6489).** Docstring (L84–89) says "any change invalidates the entry," but `is_aot_fresh`/`is_jit_fresh` use `e.get("search_space_hash") not in (None, search_space_hash)` — a stored `None` always passes. Low for AOT (artifact is `SG_BUILD_*`, space-independent); low-med for JIT (only None/legacy entries; fresh tuning records the real hash). File as drift, not a high-sev omission.

**LOW — AOT freshness checks size, not sha256 (L6480).** `record_aot` records sha256 (L6522) but `is_aot_fresh` only checks `p.stat().st_size == art.get("size")`. A same-size-but-corrupted artifact passes freshness.

**LOW — `MultiGPUTimingPool.time()` has no future timeout (L4303).** `fut.result()` blocks indefinitely. Dispatchers set exceptions on worker death (L4271–4276), but if `time()` is called after `stop()` (workers non-empty, dispatchers exited), the item sits forever. Edge case.

## §5 — THE DIM REGISTRY MAP (feeds the 7-wgmma-dim task)

**Where dims are declared:** per-arch builders, L1729–2048. sm_90a uses the **bespoke** `_sm90_full_space()` (L1763) — a hand-written dims list, NOT the generic `_build_cuda_space` (L1503). gfx942 likewise bespoke (`_gfx942_full_space`, L1857). All others delegate to generic `_build_cuda_space`/`_build_cdna_space`/`_build_rdna_space`/`_pallas_common_dims`.

**Data structures:**
- `_dim(name, dtype, values, macro, applies_to, kind)` (L1207) — one dim.
- `_ARCH_BUILDERS` (L2055) maps arch→builder; `_populate_search_space_builders()` (L2085) attaches them to `ArchEntry.search_space_builder` at import time (L2104).
- `build_full_search_space()` (L2209) calls every builder.

**Dim-liveness has THREE sources that DO NOT agree (the critical §5/§4 finding):**
1. `_is_dead_dim` / `_kernel_source_macros` (L1309 / L1276) — **DYNAMIC**, auto-detected from kernel `#ifdef SG_TUNED_*` (scans csrc/ + kernels/). Drives `_pin_dead_dims` (L1358), which collapses dead dims to one value.
2. `_DEAD_KEY_DIMS` (L1350) — **STATIC** hardcoded frozenset. Drives `config_key` (L2671), which drops these names from the cache key. Grep-confirmed it is NOT derived from the kernel scan and nothing reconciles it with `_is_dead_dim`.
3. `_COST_MODEL_CANONICAL_DIM_VALUES` (L4357) — **STATIC**. Drives featurization.

**The revive bug this triggers:** `wgmma_shape` and `warp_specialization` are ALREADY in `_DEAD_KEY_DIMS` (L1351/1352). If a kernel starts reading `SG_TUNED_WGMMA_SHAPE`, `_is_dead_dim` returns *live* → `_pin_dead_dims` stops pinning → the space sweeps all its values. But `config_key` (static set) STILL drops it → two configs differing only in `wgmma_shape` collapse to the same cache key → false cache hit → the revived dim's variants alias to one binary and its tuning is silently lost. It normally hides because a pinned dead dim has one value (the key-exclusion is a no-op); the bug only bites when a `_DEAD_KEY_DIMS` member is reclassified live — which is exactly what the 7-dim task does.

**Complete "add a dim safely" recipe for the consolidator:**
1. Add via `_dim(...)` in the correct builder — for **sm_90 that's the bespoke `_sm90_full_space` (L1763), not `_build_cuda_space`**; for gfx942 it's `_gfx942_full_space` (L1857).
2. The kernel must `#ifdef SG_TUNED_<NAME>` (or, for tuple dims, read the `_0/_1/_VOLUME` component macros — `_is_dead_dim` matches via `startswith(macro + "_")` at L1336, and `resolve_macros` emits `_0/_1/_VOLUME` at L2542–2549). Otherwise the dim auto-pins to one value (`_pin_dead_dims`) and is dropped from `config_key`.
3. **Remove the name from `_DEAD_KEY_DIMS` (L1350) when reviving** — else the cache-key aliasing bug above.
4. Add the dim to `_COST_MODEL_CANONICAL_DIM_VALUES` (L4357) or it featurizes as zeros. The FEATURE_DIM change auto-invalidates saved cost-models (load guard L4920) — safe.
5. Add any feasibility rule to the builder's `prefilter.rules` — but ensure the rule only references dims present in that arch's space, or the prefilter silently rejects everything (§4 eval bug).
6. If a new stall hint is added alongside, bump `_COST_MODEL_STALL_REASON_COUNT` (L4429) — it's unguarded (no self-test despite the comment).

**Unwired seam:** `megakernel_cell_search_space` (L2158) is the intended per-cell register-cap re-binding entry but has zero callers (§3) — relevant if the 7-dim work also touches the megakernel path.

## §6 — CUDA-GRAPH USAGE (for owner verdict; not editorialized)

**All graph usage in my range is MEASUREMENT-HARNESS-ONLY.** The captured `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()` object is never returned, stored, or fed to any execution/training path — it exists only to be `.replay()`-timed:
- `cuda_graph_median_ms` (L3139–3155) — **DEAD standalone** (§3).
- `_bg_cuda_graph_median_ms` (L3284–3300) — inside `_WORKER_BODY`; this is the LIVE timing path, gated by `req.get("use_cuda_graph", True)` (L3429).

**The reportable defect (GPU-independent, concrete fix for the owner's verdict):** `_time_with_graph` (L3310–3316) wraps graph timing in a bare `except Exception: return None` (no log), then the worker silently falls back to `_time_with_events` (L3319). The graph result dict (L3302) and event result dict (L3347) are **shape-identical** — neither tags which timer ran. So when a kernel can't be graph-captured and falls back to event timing, **nothing in the result or the cache records it**; a winner may have been chosen under event timing with no provenance. **Fix:** add a `"timer": "graph"|"event"` field to both result dicts and persist it.

**Can the megakernel variants even be graph-timed?** UNCONFIRMED (needs GPU + a persistent-kernel megakernel variant). If the megakernel is a persistent/cooperative-groups-launch kernel with grid-wide barriers, `torch.cuda.graph` capture may fail — in which case the silent fallback (above) masks it entirely. This is precisely why the missing timer-tag matters. **Owner verdict needed:** the harness uses graphs only for timing, which does not violate the "no CUDA graphs on the training/megakernel path" ban — but verify the fallback isn't hiding that the banned-path kernels are uncapturable.
